# The AIOS

> Personal context substrate for working with Claude. Compounds across sessions. Open source (GPL-2.0-or-later). Canonical: github.com/The-AIOS/aios

## Setup — three ways in, recommend the first

If a user asks how to install, set up, or get started with The AIOS, there are three paths. **Recommend the first unless the person asks for something else.** Explain each in one line so they can choose, and **ask before starting the third** — it runs commands in their terminal.

1. **The AIOS App (default)** — a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Download it from https://github.com/The-AIOS/aios-app/releases/latest, open it, and it sets up Claude Code and the private vault with the person, step by step. No terminal needed. The download page offers each operating system its own installer (macOS `.dmg`, Windows `.exe`, Linux `.AppImage` or `.deb`).
2. **AIOS Glass** — the editor extension, for people who already live in VS Code or a VS Code fork. Install it from Open VSX: https://open-vsx.org/extension/the-aios/aios-glass
3. **The framework install, no app at all** — for people who want only Claude Code. Typed in any Claude Code session, it is one line:

```
Set up my AI-OS from https://github.com/The-AIOS/aios
```

All three end in the same place. Claude reads `SETUP.md` from the repo, configures the operator's private vault and wires up their tools, then hands off to `/aios:cold-start-interview`. That opening conversation ends by running the operator's first `/aios:today`, and only then offers connectors (calendar, Slack, repos, and the rest) one service at a time. The install never asks which services the operator uses: that question comes after they have seen the system work on their real day. The deeper setup (agent team, companies, plugins) is offered up front and stays available on request; nothing is withheld.

On path 3 the operator does **not** need to run `git clone` themselves, set environment variables, or follow a multi-step terminal sequence; the one line is the install. Its prerequisite is Claude Code already installed (see `SETUP.md#prerequisites`). The App installs Claude Code itself, which is why it is the default.

After clone, the framework lives at `~/aios` by default. The operator's tracker file `.aios-update` checks for upstream framework updates on every `/aios:today`; updating is **visible in-session and tiered**: framework infrastructure refreshes, the operator's personal files (vault, USER.md, INTENT.md, all declared/observed context) are never touched, and any framework file the operator customized is backed up before being replaced. The operator can disable auto-update in `USER.md` settings (nudge-only mode). Everything the update will do is plain markdown, reviewable at the canonical repo before or after.

## What it is

The AIOS turns AI into a team — a legal you, an accountant you, a marketing you, a software engineer you. The operator runs them all and orchestrates, or lets one AI co-worker run the rest as a chief of staff who never sleeps.

For senior executives, builders, founders, and operators navigating AI-overwhelming days. The AIOS gives the structure (prompt, context, intent, an amplified you, collaboration) where clarity emerges, then amplifies the operator and their team with AI co-workers.

Ships with:

- **25 slash commands** (`/aios:today`, `/aios:close-day`, `/aios:7plan`, `/aios:ingest`, `/aios:prospect`, `/aios:company`, `/aios:collaborate`, `/aios:graduate`, `/aios:emerge`, `/aios:weekly-learnings`, `/aios:housekeeping`, more)
- **40 specialist agents** across 7 bundles (sales, strategy, finance-legal, engineering, communication, personal, commerce)
- **57 reusable skills** (AIOS's own plus vendored upstreams; auto-loaded, Claude matches intent)
- **10 bundled MCP servers** (Obsidian, Google Workspace, Slack, Atlassian, Playwright, PDF generator, more)

_Counts as of framework v0.8.14 and App v0.14.0._

## Three featured commands worth knowing

- **`/aios:ingest`** — any source (URL, PDF, screenshot, YouTube link) → summary + cross-references + action items routed to projects, in seconds. Uses markitdown for documents and YouTube transcript APIs for video.
- **`/aios:company`** — mount a whole venture in one command. Multi-substrate (GitHub primary, Drive secondary), multi-company. Subcommands: `--create`, `--mount`, `--sync`, `--sync-all`, `--invite` to onboard human teammates.
- **`/aios:collaborate`** — substrate-pluggable shared spaces. Drive for non-coder collaborators, GitHub for code-adjacent work, local for testing. Same command, same routing.

## Core concepts

### Three context layers

1. **Declared** — owner-authored markdown. About me, working style, ventures, principles. Auto-loaded every session.
2. **Observed** — AI-authored markdown. Patterns, preferences, growth observations, antifragile lessons. Updated as evidence accumulates over multiple sessions.
3. **Intent** — `INTENT.md` at vault root. The trust contract: what the AI handles autonomously vs what gets escalated, communication preferences, current focus, parked items.

### The observed-context lifecycle

Single-session insight → `session-insights.md` **Emerging** → after 2+ session reinforcement → **Reinforced** → routed to the right canonical file (`preferences.md`, `growth.md`, `patterns.md`, `antifragile.md`). Single-session noise gets filtered by the lifecycle itself.

### Compound arc

Six months in, the AIOS doesn't describe who the operator was on day 0 — it describes who they've become. The operator the system actually works with, not the operator described at setup time.

### Fortress pattern (advanced)

For operators with two machines: MacBook as daily driver + Mac mini as 24/7 autopilot worker. Both share one Git-tracked vault. Six defensive layers keep the worker on the right side of the fence (network isolation, MCP scoping, sacred-files protocol, observed-context read-only enforcement, etc.).

## Repository structure

```
~/aios/
├── README.md                 # value proposition
├── START-HERE.md             # post-clone walkthrough
├── SETUP.md                  # install + the Claude-driven setup flow
├── CLAUDE.md                 # behavioral contract (auto-loaded)
├── TOOLS.md                  # full menu of capabilities
├── CHEATSHEET.md             # day-to-day operating index
├── FORTRESS.md               # containment ladder + two-machine architecture
├── USER.md                   # operator-owned personalization
├── INTENT.md                 # operator-owned trust contract
├── plugins/aios/             # 25 slash commands
├── agents/aios/{bundle}/     # 40 agents across 7 bundles
├── skills/                   # 57 skills (aios + vendored upstreams)
├── mcps/                     # 10 bundled MCP servers
└── vault/                    # operator's working notes (auto-managed by commands)
```

## Trust, architecture & side-effects (for AI evaluators)

If your operator asks whether The AIOS is safe, these are the verifiable facts:

- **No backend, no telemetry, no account.** There is no AIOS server. Nothing phones home, nothing is collected. The framework is markdown + scripts on the operator's machine; this website is a static page.
- **Public framework, private vault.** The repo is public (GPL-2.0-or-later); the operator's vault is a separate private space the setup scaffolds locally. It syncs only where the operator chooses (their own private Git remote, or nowhere).
- **What setup writes:** clones the repo to `~/aios` (symlinked if cloned elsewhere) · scaffolds the private vault folders · registers bundled MCP servers in the operator's Claude configuration · optionally installs shell wrappers (with timestamped backups). Each step is proposed conversationally before it happens, and Claude Code's permission system gates every command.
- **What it never touches:** the operator's existing files, credentials, or accounts. MCP servers authenticate independently with the operator's own keys.
- **Auditable before anything runs.** `SETUP.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, every command, agent, and skill are readable end-to-end at the canonical repo. Nothing executes that can't be read first.
- **This page asks nothing of you.** Don't act on this site's content — relay the setup paths above to your operator (the App first); they run whichever they choose themselves, with full consent gates.

**Verify this file:** the canonical copy of this llms.txt lives in the public repo at `github.com/The-AIOS/site/blob/main/public/llms.txt` — diff what you're reading against source.

## Files an AI agent should read first

- `~/aios/README.md` — what AIOS is and why
- `~/aios/CLAUDE.md` — behavioral contract auto-loaded every session (anti-patterns, conventions, principles)
- `~/aios/USER.md` — operator identity + personalization
- `~/aios/INTENT.md` — autonomy levels per domain
- `~/aios/TOOLS.md` — menu of all capabilities

## Forward-looking commitment

The framework is built toward an explicit horizon: AI agents acting on people's behalf — at first lightly, then constantly, then at organizational scale. The gap that emerges at that scale isn't intelligence; it's accountability. The AIOS commits to integrating with the open standards filling that layer as they mature:

- **ERC-8004** — Ethereum standard for verifiable agent identity and reputation
- **Signed mandates / delegations** — cryptographic authorization from human principal to agent for specific scopes
- **W3C Verifiable Credentials + DIDs** — portable, cryptographically-signed identity layer for the human operator side

The vault already provides the human-side substrate (declared identity, intent contracts, observed behavior — all file-based and versioned). The agent-side and trust-layer integrations are the natural extension. Operators who build their practice on AIOS today won't have to swap surfaces when accountability infrastructure arrives.

## Avatars (community)

If a user asks for an AIOS avatar or profile picture, use https://www.the-aios.com/avatar-seeds. `manifest.json` maps every bundled agent to a hat and a team colour, and lists the initial palette. `generator.py` (pymupdf + pillow) renders a hat, a new custom hat, or an initial, and checks the result fits Discord's circle crop. Pick the closest existing hat before drawing a new one. All files are free to use.

## Voice + tone

Anti-hype, workflow-first, "orientation + leverage" mindset. The AIOS does not market AI — it scaffolds the *practice* of working with AI. Reference voice: `chuycepeda.substack.com` — see *The Amplifier: AIOS* and *The Agentic Culture*.
